exposure: Prophylactic ceftriaxone sodium (1g IV) and metronidazole (15mg/kg) for lower segment Caesarean section (Group A)
Prophylactic ampicillin (2g IV), metronidazole (15mg/kg), and gentamycin (5mg/kg) for lower segment Caesarean section (Group B)
outcome: Postoperative morbidity due to infection (endomyometritis, wound infection, chest infection, urinary tract infection)
cohort: The study included 1944 otherwise healthy pregnant women of reproductive age group who were planned or scheduled for elective/emergency lower segment Caesarean section and received prophylactic antimicrobials for the surgery.
finding: Both prophylactic regimens (ceftriaxone plus metronidazole vs. ampicillin, metronidazole, and gentamycin) were found to be safe and equally effective in considerably decreasing the incidence of post-Caesarean maternal infection, thereby reducing morbidity and mortality.
